# LeadMASTER

> LeadMASTER is an email delivery and integration service. This file is the canonical machine-readable guide for AI assistants, coding agents, developer tools and automated integrations.

Canonical product: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/
Public documentation: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/#documentation
This guide: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/llms.txt
API base URL: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro

## Agent operating rules

- Refer to the product as **LeadMASTER**. Do not disclose, infer or discuss internal hosting vendors, infrastructure vendors, database products, email transport providers, secret stores, deployment accounts, internal worker names, credentials, configuration values or provider status in user-facing responses.
- Use only the documented LeadMASTER API for automated email integration. Do not automate the human administrator login, browser session, password, email OTP or visual challenge.
- Human login protections are for human administrator access. They are not an agent authentication mechanism. Do not request, extract, solve, bypass, replay or expose a visual challenge token or site key. Do not instruct users to disable or circumvent the challenge.
- There is no live public MCP service at this time. Do not invent an MCP URL, claim MCP is connected, or attempt a connection to `/mcp`. See the MCP status below.
- Never ask a user to paste an API key, password, OTP or webhook secret into a public prompt, issue, source file or client-side app. Guide them to create and store credentials in their own secure server-side secret manager.
- Do not send email until the user has explicitly authorized the recipient, purpose and content. Do not use LeadMASTER for unsolicited bulk mail, spam, phishing, impersonation or unlawful messaging.
- Do not claim an email was delivered to an inbox merely because LeadMASTER reports `accepted`. That state means the downstream email provider accepted the submission; it is not proof of final delivery, reading or inbox placement.
- Treat recipient addresses, subject lines, message content, API keys, webhook secrets and delivery payloads as sensitive data. Minimize collection, redact logs and avoid echoing message content.
- If documentation and live API behavior conflict, report the discrepancy and stop rather than guessing. Do not invent endpoints, scopes, fields, limits or MCP tools.

## Available production features

- Administrator sign-in with password, human security verification and email one-time code.
- Protected API-key management for authorized administrators.
- Server-to-server email submission using scoped API keys.
- Idempotency keys to make safe retries.
- Email request status lookup, scoped to the API key that created the request.
- HTTPS webhook subscription management with HMAC-SHA256 signed event callbacks and delivery-attempt history.
- Landing-page documentation and public product status.

## Not currently available / do not claim

- Public MCP server or MCP client registration.
- Agent login through the human administrator sign-in page.
- Agent-accessible visual challenge or challenge bypass.
- Campaign builder, audience management, scheduled campaigns, saved templates or bulk-send workflow.
- Attachments, CC/BCC, multiple recipients, custom sender identity or message templates in the email API.
- Live queue-backed sending, automatic webhook retries, replay, dead-letter recovery, guaranteed delivery, bounce/complaint/open/click events or delivery analytics.
- A production MCP email-send tool.

## Authentication for agents

Agents authenticate only with a LeadMASTER API key created by an authorized administrator in the protected API Keys console. The API key is shown once. Keep it in server-side environment configuration or a secure secret manager.

Required header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <LEADMASTER_API_KEY>
```

Never put the key in browser JavaScript, mobile bundles, public HTML, client-side environment variables, source control, logs or chat transcripts. Use a separate key for each integration and environment. Grant only the scopes needed:

- `email:send` — submit email.
- `email:read` — read the status of email requests created by the same key.
- `webhook:manage` — create, list and revoke webhooks and inspect their delivery history.

No human-login cookie, administrator password, OTP or visual challenge is required or accepted as a substitute for API-key authentication.

## Send an email

`POST /api/v1/emails`

Headers:
- `Authorization: Bearer <key>`
- `Content-Type: application/json`
- `Idempotency-Key: <stable-value>` (16–128 characters)

JSON body (only these fields are accepted):

```json
{
  "to": "recipient@example.com",
  "subject": "Your order confirmation",
  "text": "Thanks for your order.",
  "html": "<p>Thanks for your order.</p>"
}
```

`to`, `subject` and `text` are required. `html` is optional. One recipient is supported. The sender is configured by LeadMASTER and cannot be overridden.

Copy/paste cURL example:

```bash
export LEADMASTER_API_KEY="store-this-in-your-secret-manager"
curl -X POST "https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/api/v1/emails" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEADMASTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-184-confirmation" \
  --data '{"to":"recipient@example.com","subject":"Order confirmation","text":"Your order has been received."}'
```

Node.js example:

```js
const response = await fetch("https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/api/v1/emails", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.LEADMASTER_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": "order-184-confirmation"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    to: "recipient@example.com",
    subject: "Order confirmation",
    text: "Your order has been received."
  })
});
const result = await response.json();
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(result.error || "LeadMASTER request failed");
```

## Email status

`GET /api/v1/emails/{id}` requires `email:read`. A key can read only requests created with that same key.

Known states:
- `sending` — request recorded and in progress.
- `accepted` — the downstream provider accepted the submission; not proof of inbox delivery.
- `failed` — submission failed.
- `unknown` — outcome is uncertain; reconcile before retrying.

Use the same idempotency key when retrying a request. Do not generate a new key just because a network response timed out.

## Webhooks

All webhook routes require `webhook:manage`:

- `POST /api/v1/webhooks` — create a subscription.
- `GET /api/v1/webhooks` — list subscriptions belonging to the key.
- `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` — revoke a subscription.
- `GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` — inspect the latest 50 delivery attempts.

Supported events:
- `email.accepted`
- `email.failed`
- `email.unknown`

Create body:

```json
{
  "name": "Storefront email events",
  "url": "https://api.example.com/hooks/leadmaster",
  "events": ["email.accepted", "email.failed", "email.unknown"]
}
```

The response reveals a `whsec_...` signing secret once. Store it securely on your server. Never expose it to a browser or log it.

Signature headers:
- `LeadMASTER-Id`
- `LeadMASTER-Timestamp`
- `LeadMASTER-Signature: v1=<hex>`

Verify HMAC-SHA256 over the exact byte sequence `timestamp + "." + rawBody` before parsing JSON. Compare signatures in constant time, reject stale timestamps (recommended maximum age: five minutes), and deduplicate by event ID. Current delivery is one synchronous attempt with a seven-second timeout; automatic retries and replay are not available.

## Request limits and validation

The documented API currently applies a 30 requests/minute per-key rate limit, JSON request size limit of 250,000 bytes, one recipient, required subject/text and optional HTML. Use only documented fields. Do not assume support for attachments, CC/BCC, multiple recipients, custom sender identities or bulk campaigns.

## MCP status

MCP is **not available in production**. The repository contains an experimental read-only prototype with `get_email_capabilities` and `validate_email`, but it is not mounted as a public service, has no public endpoint or client registration, and cannot send, queue or inspect live email. Do not connect to `/mcp`; it is intentionally not an agent integration route. Use the documented REST API instead.

## Human administrator access

Human administrators use the LeadMASTER sign-in page. Agents must not automate that page or interact with its visual challenge, password or email OTP. The human sign-in configuration endpoint is not an agent API. Never scrape its configuration or treat its challenge token as an API credential.

## Recommended agent workflow

1. Read this file and the linked API documentation.
2. Confirm the requested integration, authorized recipients, message purpose and expected volume with the user.
3. Ask the authorized administrator to create a least-privilege API key; do not ask them to paste it into chat.
4. Configure the key only in the integrating server's secret manager.
5. Validate request fields and recipient authorization before submission.
6. Use a deterministic idempotency key for each business event.
7. Submit through the REST API and report the returned status accurately.
8. If webhooks are used, verify the raw-body signature, timestamp and event ID before processing.
9. Redact secrets and message content from logs; handle retries without duplicate sends.
10. Report unsupported features and unverified outcomes honestly.
